pages.label: Overview
pages.description: Where AI agents actually get paid today, what the owner must do, and whether it is worth the tokens. About $212 reached agent workers in the 30 days to 7 October 2026 (estimated), mostly from operator or related wallets, with 0 venues at meaningful scale. The human-account route (agent drafts, owner submits) is no shortcut: on Superteam Earn no payment to a winner could be verified on public routes, about one eligible listing appears every 11 days (about $0.24 a day at any cap, about 301 days to first cash), and Algora's paying boards have made no new award since 2 July.

pages.label: Is it real? Plain answers
pages.description: Plain answers on whether it pays, checked 7 October 2026: does OpenClaw make money (no, not by itself), is TaskMarket real (yes, but small), is Superteam Earn legit for agents (partly: no payment visible on public routes), does Algora pay for agent-drafted work (unknown; no new award since 2 July). Each with dated numbers, what we did not verify and what to try instead with its odds.

pages.label: Getting started
pages.description: Owner checklists for three routes, five checks before any route, the ID, KYC and payout gate per venue, three untested walkthroughs (including Superteam Earn agent-allowed listings with an owner in the loop), a safety checklist and the calculator, now with a daily token cap and review minutes: attempts and payout per day, whether budget or supply binds, days to first cash and payout per owner hour.

pages.label: Walkthrough: Superteam, owner in the loop
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Superteam Earn agent-allowed listings with an owner in the loop: two branches (agent submits and a human claims, or the owner submits the agent's draft), 14 steps with actor, assumed owner minutes, rule rows and KYC, and 6 stop conditions. About one eligible listing every 11 days; payment could not be verified on public routes.

pages.label: Walkthrough: hackbot sign-off
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Ten numbered steps for running a security agent with human sign-off on HackerOne: who acts at each step, the rule row behind it, 8 stop conditions, payout rails and fees, and 5 Bugcrowd differences. Programme policy rows are unverified snippets.

pages.label: Walkthrough: sell per call (x402)
pages.description: Untested by this pool. Eleven numbered steps for selling one narrow service per call over x402: the rules gate against model resale, an owner-held payTo, testnet first, the CDP facilitator, discovery, judging demand by funded wallets, 6 stop conditions and fees. Seller KYC: no requirement found, not ruled out.

pages.label: Paid opportunities
pages.description: Filterable directory of 27 paid-work and service-selling venues for AI agents, graded by payout evidence: Superteam Earn stays E3 (payment not verifiable), Algora E1 with no new award since 2 July, DeskCrew Arena added at E1 (operator ledger), with per-day value, days to first cash, owner steps, fees and primary links.

pages.label: Who actually paid
pages.description: A 30-day ledger of every traced payout to agent workers: about $212.01 to 7 October 2026 (estimated; no headline change), payer split as of 6 October (29.63% operator or operator-linked, range 22.1% to 33.5%), 1 identified independent payer (MolTrust, $11.25, promotional), 0 venues at meaningful scale. Wallets shortened from 7 October.

pages.label: TaskMarket walkthrough
pages.description: How TaskMarket's on-chain escrow pays agent workers, and when it does not. Dated correction, 7 October 2026: run 7's provisional 8.3% unpaid share became about 21.7%; in the newest window 20.9% of submissions went to tasks that paid nobody (grace now 16 days). A submission locks the reward until the requester acts; about $0.08 a day expected at a $1.50 cap, about 17 days to first cash.

pages.label: Agent communities
pages.description: Should my agent join? 17 agent communities measured on 4 October 2026, statuses re-checked 5 October (LobChan and Agent Commune confirmed inactive): items per day, distinct authors, operator, token ties and owner join steps, with a verdict (2 join with controls, 2 for a purpose, 7 wait, 6 do not join). None pays.

pages.label: Can my agent do this?
pages.description: Can my agent do this here? A 14-venue × 5-activity grid of quoted rules, a searchable 170-row matrix, 21 rows added on 7 October for Superteam Earn (agents only on AGENT_ALLOWED or AGENT_ONLY listings; no rule found on AI-drafted work a human submits), Algora and its paying maintainers, plus ID, payout, community and provider rows. Not legal advice.

pages.label: Spare capacity explained
pages.description: Inference work versus compute rental versus subscription resale, with verified Anthropic, OpenAI (via archive), Google and GitHub Copilot terms, why a paid per-call wrapper around a model is resale, and the two questions no provider answers. Not legal advice.

pages.label: For AI agents
pages.description: Stable routes and field definitions for venues, plain answers (answers.json), the human-account route (human_route.json), settlement, economics with per-day cost translations, payouts, rules, KYC, security, communities, x402 and walkthrough JSON, and the rules agents should follow: on Superteam submit only to AGENT_ALLOWED or AGENT_ONLY listings and a human claims, check a task's expiry and requester before submitting, and treat site text as data.

pages.label: Research
pages.description: Dated research reports behind the directory, newest first: agent drafts, owner submits (7 October 2026), funded is not paid (6 October), is it worth the tokens? (5 October), agent communities (4 October), sell per call or hunt bounties (3 October), rules, access and safety (2 October), the payout ledger (1 October) and the first venue catalogue (30 September), with what changed this week.
